subject: general
question: Select the correct option related to the function of auxin in plants.

options.text: Helps the cells to grow longer

solution:
The correct answer is __**Helps the cells to grow longer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Auxins** are a group of plant hormones that play a crucial role in the elongation of plant cells in the shoot system.
 
• They are primarily produced in the **apical meristems** of the plant and move downwards to stimulate cell elongation.
 
• Auxins help in the **regulation of phototropism and gravitropism**, allowing plants to grow towards light and against gravity.
 
• They also aid in the differentiation of vascular tissues, which is essential for the transport of water and nutrients throughout the plant.
 
• Another key function of auxins is to **promote root initiation** and development, which is vital for plant stability and nutrient uptake.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phototropism**

 
 
• It is the growth of an organism in response to a light stimulus.
 
• Auxins accumulate on the shaded side of the plant, causing cells on that side to elongate more and the plant to bend towards the light.
 
 
 
• **Gravitropism**
 
 
• It is the orientation of a plant or other organism in response to gravity.
 
• Roots exhibit positive gravitropism (growing downward), while shoots exhibit negative gravitropism (growing upward).
 
 
 
• **Apical Dominance**
 
 
• It is the phenomenon where the main, central stem of the plant is dominant over other side stems.
 
• Auxins produced in the apical bud suppress the growth of lateral buds, thus maintaining apical dominance.
 
 
 
• **Root Initiation**
 
 
• Auxins play a pivotal role in the formation of roots from cuttings and other vegetative parts of the plant.
 
• They stimulate the cells in the stem to differentiate into root cells, aiding in plant propagation.
